now.title: Arm V1 build (UK)
now.note: Start the follower arm in the UK: order servos and board, weigh the filament spool, print a test part, then the rest.
now.details: Decided 10 Nov: build starts in the UK, two months before Brazil. Follower arm only, no leader arm (pod picking is structured, so scripted moves will do). No camera yet: the servos report their own angles. Order: six 12 V STS3215 servos plus one Waveshare board, from Amazon UK if under about £135, otherwise ArmDojo. 12 V 5 A supply: check home first. Print ahead of the motors; the SO-101 files are made for the STS3215. After assembly: calibrate, teach poses, then a mock pick-and-place on the table (tray to printed pipe hole).

now.title: Project hub
now.note: The site is the project's home; CONTEXT.md is the start point for every session.
now.details: Live: homepage, roadmap with a page per item, decisions and notes, shopping list, history, drawings, shared burger menu. docs/CONTEXT.md holds the big picture and points to the JSON files, so nothing is written twice.

now.title: UK vs Brazil sourcing
now.note: Small, valuable electronics from the UK in the cabin bag; bulky, generic parts bought in Brazil.
now.details: Brazilian import tax can roughly double the price of electronics, so the servos, driver board, USB cable and a power supply that works on Brazil voltage go in the cabin bag. The pipe, tank, plywood, filament, N20 motors and the Bambu A1 printer are bought in Brazil. Duty-free allowance is US$1,000 by air; keep receipts.

next.note: A small web app to record named poses and play them back as sequences.
next.details: Runs in Chrome and talks to the servo board over USB using Web Serial, so it can be built and hosted through Viber. Needs the Feetech servo protocol written for the browser (LeRobot is Python). Grows into the real control software later.
